basic_information.official_title: AN ACT CREATING THE BANGSAMORO SPORTS COMMISSION, PROVIDING FOR ITS MANDATE, POWERS, AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Atty. Ali Pangalian M. Balindong, Speaker
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation in the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Creates the region's sports commission — with a commissioner for each province, seats for indigenous and settler communities, and an unusual mandate: to make sports a tool for peace and transitional justice.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: Section 20, Article IX of the Organic Law provides for a sports commission. The act builds it and gives it a framing beyond athletics — supporting indigenous games and martial arts, and researching sport as an instrument against criminality, drugs and violent extremism.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: A commission attached to the Office of the Chief Minister becomes the policy-making and coordinating body for all amateur sports in the region. It can accredit sports clubs, sanction associations, athletes and officials, and require every ministry to submit its sports plan, budget and implementation reports.
who_will_be_affected: Athletes and sports officials in the region, who fall under the Commission's regulatory power
Sports clubs and people's organisations, which the Commission accredits
Non-Moro indigenous peoples and settler communities, holding two ex-officio seats
Out-of-school youth, marginalised children and persons with disability, engaged through the youth commission
Every ministry with a sports programme, which must submit plans, budgets and reports
Schools, whose sports programme stays with the education ministry with the Commission assisting
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2022 — the enacted copy is date-stamped 10 May 2022, about 2 years after Parliament passed it, effective 15 days after publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. There is a commissioner for your province, the Commission can accredit your sports club, and it is expressly directed to support indigenous games and martial arts — not only the sports that travel to national meets.
in_practice: A Chairman and four regular Commissioners representing Basilan with Lamitan City, Lanao del Sur with Marawi City, Maguindanao with Cotabato City and the 63 barangays, Sulu, and Tawi-Tawi
Two ex-officio Commissioners for Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples and settler communities
Fixed seven-year terms — long for a Philippine commission
Commissioners need only be 21 years old, resident in the region for 5 years, and a registered voter of the subdivision they represent
The Commission accredits sports clubs and people's organisations
It can impose sanctions on sports associations, teams, athletes and officials for violating its rules
It coordinates with the education ministry on Palarong Pambansa and the regional athletic association meet
₱9,500,000 total initial funding — the smallest of the region's commissions

for_specific_groups.Athletes: The Commission provides incentives, recognition and awards as far as the rules of amateurism permit, procures and distributes sportswear and equipment for the regional pool, and can refer individual athletes needing help to regional or national agencies.
for_specific_groups.Indigenous and traditional sports: Supporting indigenous games and martial arts is written into the policy section, and research on promoting and preserving indigenous sports is among the Commission's functions.
for_specific_groups.Non-Moro indigenous peoples and settler: Two ex-officio commissioners, designated by the Chief Minister from three nominees each submitted by the indigenous peoples' ministry and the settler communities office. They must be organic personnel of the Bangsamoro Government and receive per diems rather than a salary.
for_specific_groups.Out-of-school youth, marginalised childr: The Commission works with the Bangsamoro Youth Commission to engage organisations serving you and develop your potential in sports.
for_specific_groups.Sports clubs: You can seek accreditation, and you fall under the Commission's sanctioning power.
for_specific_groups.LGUs: The Commission assists in setting up provincial, municipal, barangay and school district sports councils, and in promoting sports at community level.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The whole BARMM, with commissioners representing five major political subdivisions.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: In force since 2022, though the act sat about 2 years between passage and approval.
what_you_can_do: Seek accreditation for your sports club or organisation
Approach the commissioner for your province
If you run indigenous games or martial arts programmes, these are expressly within the Commission's mandate to encourage and support
Ask your LGU about a local sports promotion and development council — the Commission is directed to assist in establishing them
watch_out_for: ₱9.5 million total initial funding, against ₱30 million each for the Women and Youth Commissions.

The act lists Sulu among the represented subdivisions; the region's parliamentary districting acts of 2025 and 2026 no longer include the province, and no act read by this registry addresses the effect on this Commission's composition.
The enacted copy is date-stamped 10 May 2022 — roughly 2 years after Parliament passed it in September 2020.
Commissioners hold policy-making powers only; executive authority sits with the Chairperson and the Executive Director.
Ex-officio commissioners must be existing Bangsamoro Government personnel, which limits who the indigenous and settler communities can nominate.

key_terms_explained.Amateur sports: Sport played without payment. The Commission is the policy body for all amateur sports development programmes and institutions in the region.
key_terms_explained.Indigenous games: Recreational activities originating from a particular cultural group — part of a people's heritage, preserving traditions and stories.
key_terms_explained.Ex-officio: Holding a seat by virtue of another office. Here the two ex-officio commissioners receive per diems rather than a salary.
key_terms_explained.BARMMAA: The regional athletic association meet through which the region's school athletes qualify onward.
key_terms_explained.Sports Advisory Council: A council advising the Chairman on capital expenditure priorities, grants to sporting societies, sports development, international competitions and the use of facilities.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed 17 September 2020; the enacted copy carries a Chief Minister's approval date-stamped 5/10/22.

benefits.headline: A sports commission with a provincial commissioner each, indigenous and settler seats, and a mandate reaching into peace work.

direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Athletes and sports organisations across the region

direct_benefits.benefit: Accreditation for sports clubs and people's organisations
Sportswear, equipment, instruments and tools for training the regional pool of athletes
Incentives, recognition and awards for deserving athletes and supporters
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Athletes and those supporting sports development
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Section 11(b)(9), as far as amateurism rules permit

direct_benefits.benefit: Support for indigenous games and martial arts
Programmes reaching out-of-school youth, marginalised children and persons with disability
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Section 11(b)(3), with the Bangsamoro Youth Commission

direct_benefits.benefit: Sports facilities and centres in strategic places

indirect_benefits: Local sports promotion and development councils at provincial, municipal, barangay and school district level
Linkages with the Philippine Sports Commission and foreign sports bodies
Research on sport as an instrument against criminality, drugs and violent extremism
Ministries required to submit sports plans, budgets and implementation reports
limitations: ₱9.5 million initial funding for a region-wide mandate.
School sports remain with the education ministry, with the Commission assisting.
The Commission's regulatory reach is over amateur sport, not professional.

for_citizens: None imposed on the public. Sports associations, teams, athletes and officials are subject to the Commission's policies, rules and regulations, and may be sanctioned for violating them.
for_ministries: Submit sports plans and budgets, and regular reports on implementation and utilisation, when the Commission requires them
Implement the sports promotion and development programmes indicated in their budgets
MBHTE formulates and implements the school sports development programme with the Commission's assistance
All heads of ministries, agencies and offices are enjoined to render full assistance to the Commission

what_is_prohibited: The act creates no offence. It empowers the Commission to impose sanctions on regional sports associations, institutions, bodies, teams, athletes and sports officials for violating its policies, rules and regulations.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no criminal offence, fine or imprisonment.
penalties.administrative: Sanctions imposed by the Commission on sports associations, institutions, bodies, teams, athletes and officials for violation of its policies, rules and regulations.

where_to_complain.oversight: Bangsamoro Sports Commission, attached to the Office of the Chief Minister, under the Chief Minister's general supervision
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no formal complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A community wants its traditional game supported rather than replaced by imported sports. The policy section directs the government to encourage and support indigenous games and martial arts, and research on preserving them is a Commission function.

A youth group outside the school system wants access to training. The Commission is directed to work with the Bangsamoro Youth Commission to engage organisations dealing with out-of-school youth, marginalised children and persons with disability.

A ministry budgets for a sports programme and never delivers it. The Commission may require any ministry to submit its sports plan and budget along with regular reports on implementation and utilisation.

key_provisions: Sections 1–3 — Short title: “The Bangsamoro Sports Commission Act of 2020”. Policy: promote physical education and encourage sports programmes, league competitions and amateur sports, including training for regional, national and international competitions; develop innovative and productive individuals, promote sportsmanship, and “encourage and support indigenous games, martial arts and amateur sports”; and recognise the diverse cultures of the region, considering gender, culture and religious sensitivity. Indigenous games are defined as recreational activities originating from a particular cultural group, important to a people's heritage and preserving age-old traditions and stories.

Sections 4–6 — The Bangsamoro Sports Commission is created pursuant to Section 20, Article IX of RA 11054, attached to the Office of the Chief Minister under the Chief Minister's general supervision. It exercises corporate powers, may sue and be sued, and is the policy-making and coordinating body of all amateur sports development programmes and institutions in the Bangsamoro — except the school sports development programme, which MBHTE formulates and implements with the Commission's assistance. Its mandate is to formulate policy, promote, regulate, coordinate and implement sports programmes and, “as a policy, make sure that sports is a tool for peace and transitional justice”.

Sections 7–10 — Composition: a Chairman and four regular Commissioners drawn from Basilan including Lamitan City, Lanao del Sur including Marawi City, Maguindanao including Cotabato City and the 63 barangays of North Cotabato, Sulu, and Tawi-Tawi; plus two ex-officio Commissioners representing Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples and settler communities, designated by the Chief Minister from three nominees submitted by the Ministry of Indigenous Peoples' Affairs and the Office for Settler Communities respectively, who must be organic personnel of the Bangsamoro Government and serve no more than 7 years. The Chief Minister appoints for fixed seven-year terms. Qualifications: Filipino citizen, proven integrity and independence, at least 21 years old, resident of the region for at least 5 years, registered voter of the subdivision represented, experience in positions of responsibility and leadership in government or registered sports organisations, and no conviction for moral turpitude; a majority of Commissioners must hold a bachelor's degree. The Chairperson receives Salary Grade 28 and regular Commissioners Salary Grade 27; ex-officio Commissioners receive per diems only.

Section 11 — Powers. On plan and policy-making: prepare the Bangsamoro Sports and Development Plan; recommend sports policies for legislation; research sports development including the promotion and preservation of indigenous sports; research the rights and welfare of Bangsamoro athletes; undertake research “in making sports as instrument to fight against criminalities, drugs, and violent extremism; and as a vehicle for peace”; pilot special programmes; and make sports a tool for peace and transitional justice. On coordination and promotion: maintain linkages with the Philippine Sports Commission and foreign bodies; coordinate with MBHTE on Palarong Pambansa, the regional athletic association meet and other competitions; engage, with the Bangsamoro Youth Commission, organisations dealing with youth, out-of-school youth, marginalised children, persons with disability and other vulnerable sectors; convene public and private sports bodies; assist in establishing regional, provincial, municipal, barangay and school district sports promotion and development councils; assist LGUs in community-level sports; provide incentives, recognition and awards as permissible under the rules of amateurism; refer athletes needing assistance to regional and national agencies; and establish and manage fully-equipped sports facilities in strategic places. On regulation: impose sanctions on any regional sports association, institution, body, entity or team, including athletes and sports officials, for violation of its policies, rules and regulations; accredit sports clubs and people's organisations; procure and distribute sportswear, equipment and tools for the regional pool of athletes; delineate areas of responsibility across sectors; and monitor and ensure compliance by Bangsamoro Government agencies, requiring all ministries, agencies and offices to submit their sports plan and budget and regular reports on implementation and utilisation.

Sections 12–24 — Structure: a Commission Proper, the Office of the Chairperson and an Office of the Secretariat. The Commission Proper — the Chairperson, four regular and two ex-officio Commissioners — is the highest policy and decision-making body, meeting without prior call every first and third Monday, transacting business by majority with a majority quorum, and promulgating its internal rules within 30 days of its first meeting. Commissioners hold policy-making powers only and exercise no executive functions unless designated officer-in-charge. The Secretariat is headed by an Executive Director at Salary Grade 26 with three divisions — Policy, Research and Development; Regulatory, Promotion and Coordination; and Financial and Administrative — each headed by a Division Chief at Salary Grade 25. The Commission may call on any Bangsamoro Government entity for assistance, and all heads of ministries, agencies and offices are enjoined to render full cooperation.

Sections 25–29 — Appropriations: ₱6,500,000 for Personnel Services, ₱1,500,000 for Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses and ₱1,500,000 for Capital Outlay, from the Miscellaneous Personnel Benefits Fund and the Contingent Fund under the 2020 Bangsamoro Appropriations Act, with subsequent requirements in the annual appropriations act. Transitory: of the first members appointed, the Chairperson holds office for 7 years, two regular commissioners for five and the remaining two for three. Effective 15 days after publication in the Official Gazette or at least one newspaper of general circulation in the region.

Its provincial-representation model with two voting-adjacent ex-officio seats for Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples and settler communities mirrors BAA 8 (Women Commission) and BAA 10 (Youth Commission), and it works with the Youth Commission on out-of-school youth and vulnerable sectors. citizen_questions.q: Is there a commissioner for my province?
citizen_questions.a: Yes. A Chairman and four regular Commissioners are drawn from Basilan with Lamitan City, Lanao del Sur with Marawi City, Maguindanao with Cotabato City and the 63 barangays, Sulu, and Tawi-Tawi.
Yes. Encouraging and supporting indigenous games and martial arts is written into the policy section, and research on promoting and preserving indigenous sports is a Commission function.

citizen_questions.q: Can my sports club get accredited?
citizen_questions.a: Yes. Section 11(c)(2) empowers the Commission to accredit sports clubs and people's organisations operating in the Bangsamoro engaged in the protection and promotion of sports.

The Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education formulates and implements the school sports development programme, with the Commission assisting within the framework of the regional and national sports development programme.

citizen_questions.q: Are indigenous and settler communities represented?
citizen_questions.a: Yes — two ex-officio Commissioners, designated by the Chief Minister from three nominees each submitted by the Ministry of Indigenous Peoples' Affairs and the Office for Settler Communities. They must be organic personnel of the Bangsamoro Government and receive per diems rather than a salary.

citizen_questions.q: How much money does it have?
citizen_questions.a: ₱9.5 million initially — ₱6.5M for salaries, ₱1.5M for operating expenses and ₱1.5M for capital outlay. That is the smallest initial appropriation of the region's commissions; the Women and Youth Commissions each received ₱30 million.

display_header.what_this_does: Creates the region's sports commission, with a commissioner per province and a mandate to support indigenous games and use sport for peace.
display_header.who_it_affects: Athletes · sports clubs · indigenous and settler communities · out-of-school youth

views.simple: Creates the Bangsamoro Sports Commission as the policy body for amateur sport in the region — a commissioner for each province, ex-officio seats for Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples and settler communities, power to accredit clubs and sanction associations and athletes, an express mandate to support indigenous games and martial arts, and a directive to treat sport as a tool for peace and transitional justice.
